integrity: The proof is analytic. The three-stage scheme is eliminated exactly, the one-step matrix is reduced to tensor resolvents, and entry signs are classified by disjoint coordinate-difference cases. A standalone exact-rational checker replays the two-by-two-by-two counterexample and finite determinant consequences; it is not used as a substitute for the universal proof.
scientific_limitations: The theorem covers the original three-stage first-order Douglas–Rachford heat scheme on rectangular tensor grids with homogeneous Dirichlet data and at least two interior points per coordinate. It does not cover nonhomogeneous boundary forcing, variable coefficients, irregular domains, intermediate-stage positivity, the later 1962 second-order three-dimensional method, or Douglas–Gunn variants.
title: Exact positivity region for the three-dimensional Douglas–Rachford heat scheme
